plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag/time-to-settle, which set controller sign, feedforward level for 0.5, and required integral/settling time.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.231 with short lag (tens of s) toward ~0.35-0.50, with positive early slope flattening over 300 s; slope at end indicates how close to equilibrium.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests H4/H2: whether output decays at u=0, how fast, and to what ambient level, which sets controller need for steady heating and integral time; long 480 s hold also separates noise from trend.
experiments.expected_observation: If heat-loss hypothesis is right, y will decay from ~0.47 toward ~0.10-0.20 over 480 s with curved exponential shape, ~50% of drop in first ~100-150 s, plus +/-0.02 sensor scatter; flat hold or rise would falsify H4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Tests H5/H6 linearity and steady-state gain: a second amplitude 0.4 vs 0.3 separates linear from saturating response and estimates input needed to hold 0.5, which sets feedforward and integral authority for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will rise from ~0.12 with short lag toward ~0.6-0.7 equilibrium, reaching ~0.5-0.6 after 280 s with flattening but still positive end slope; +/-0.03 scatter. Flat or falling trace would falsify H1/H5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 and tests linearity/symmetry by approaching target from above; distinguishes whether u~0.33 holds 0.5 versus needing <=0.30 or >=0.38, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order hypothesis is right, y will decay from ~0.54 toward ~0.48-0.52 over 140 s with curved flattening and end slope near zero, plus +/-0.025 scatter; continued rise above 0.56 would falsify estimated gain/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 by approaching from above at 0.27; separates u*~0.275 holding band versus needing <=0.25 or >=0.30, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient ~0.15 and K~1.28 is right, y will decay from ~0.557 toward ~0.49-0.51 over 175 s with curved flattening, reaching ~0.51-0.53 with still slightly negative end slope, plus +/-0.03 scatter/outliers; continued flat at ~0.57 or rise would falsify estimated u*~0.275 and H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 to within ~0.01 by approaching from above at 0.25, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority to stay in 0.475-0.525 band.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient~0.15, K~1.3, tau~150s is right, y will decay from ~0.526 toward ~0.48-0.51 equilibrium, reaching ~0.50-0.52 after 200s with flattening slope near zero, plus +/-0.03 scatter/outliers; flat hold at ~0.53 or continued rise would falsify estimated u*~0.26 and H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state input for y=0.5 to within ~0.01 by testing 0.26 from just below band, separating u*~0.26 holding band versus needing <=0.25 or >=0.27, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with ambient~0.15, K~1.35, tau~150s is right, y will rise slowly from ~0.477 toward ~0.50-0.51 equilibrium, reaching ~0.49-0.51 after 200s with flattening slope near zero, plus +/-0.03 scatter; flat hold far below 0.48 or rise above 0.55 would falsify estimated u*~0.26.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguishes faster outflow (faster u=0 fall) from pure weaker actuator (u=0 fall unchanged from E2) and directly measures dead-time from last command change to start of fall, which sets required integral time and whether feedforward gain or loss coefficient must be re-identified for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-gain hypothesis (C1) is right, y will hold near 0.46-0.47 for ~20-50 s while prior ~0.40 commands flush (delay), then fall as in E2 toward ~0.12-0.18, about 50% of drop in first ~150 s, reaching ~0.30-0.35 by 150 s, ~0.20 by 300 s, ~0.15 by 480 s plus +/-0.03 scatter. Faster fall to <0.25 by ~150 s or lower final level would favor faster-outflow C2; continued flat or rise would favor large delay C3.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New steady-state heater gain and new u* to hold 0.5, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority; heating from 0.18 at same u=0.4 as E3 gives direct gain comparison and approach rate to separate weaker gain from faster loss.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-gain C1 is right (K'~0.7-0.8, ambient~0.15, tau~120-180s), y will rise from ~0.18 toward ~0.42-0.46 equilibrium, reaching ~0.35-0.42 after 270 s with flattening end slope, plus +/-0.03 scatter. Rise to >0.50 and still rising would favor no gain change; much faster flattening below ~0.38 would favor faster-outflow C2; no rise for >100 s would favor large-delay C3.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New steady-state input u* to hold 0.5 after change and high-u gain linearity, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority to stay in 0.475-0.525 band.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-gain C1 (K'~0.6-0.75, ambient~0.15-0.16, tau~120-180s) is right, y will rise from ~0.40 toward ~0.51-0.55 equilibrium, reaching ~0.46-0.50 after 130s with positive but flattening slope ~0.0004-0.0008/s plus +/-0.03 scatter; rise to >0.58 and still steep would favor no gain change; flat <0.43 would favor faster-loss C2 or large-delay C3.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New steady-state input u* to hold 0.5 after gain loss, which sets controller feedforward and integral authority to stay in 0.475-0.525 band.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-gain C1/C5 (K'~0.70-0.73, ambient~0.15-0.16, tau~120-180s, u*~0.47-0.50) is right, y will hold essentially flat from ~0.498 toward ~0.50-0.51 over 110 s with slope near zero, plus +/-0.03 scatter. Continued rise toward >0.56 at ~0.0007/s would favor no gain change; fall toward <0.46 would favor faster-loss C2 or u* >0.52.

ledger.statement: Steady-state y is monotonically increasing in u pre and post but post level much lower: pre u=0.3->~0.47, u=0.4->~0.54 rising, u=0.27->0.527, u=0.26->0.483; post u=0.4->~0.40-0.44 flattening from 0.174 over 270s, u=0.55->0.496 rising toward ~0.55 after 130s.

Response has lag/inertia tau ~120-180s with short dead-time tens of s: E2 63% decay ~170s, E1/E3 still rising after 280-300s, E8 fall starts in ~16-24s, E9 rise starts in ~30-40s, E10 rise within ~6-9s of 0.4->0.55 similar to pre-change.
No large dead zone at operating levels: u=0.25 to 0.55 all produce measurable heating/holding >0.35, with ordered steady levels pre and post change.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward room level ~0.10-0.20 due to heat loss: E2 0.469 to 0.147 mean in 480s, E8 0.41 to 0.157 mean in 480s with similar curve, rather than holding.
Pre-change static gain is approximately linear with (y_ss-ambient)/u ~1.27-1.40 with ambient ~0.15: predicts ~0.49 at 0.25, ~0.49-0.50 at 0.26, ~0.53 at 0.27, ~0.57 at 0.33 as observed.
Pre-change steady-state input to hold target y=0.5 was ~0.26-0.27 centered ~0.265, because u=0.33 holds 0.571, u=0.27 holds 0.527, u=0.26 holds 0.483 in-band, u=0.25 holds 0.466-0.49 just below.
Sensor noise/outliers are substantial ~0.02-0.05 requiring averaging: E2/E3/E5/E6/E8/E9/E10 show +/-0.03 scatter and 0.04-0.08 dips, so only trends >0.05 over 100s are reliable dynamics.

Change includes weaker actuator (~45% gain reduction to K'~0.70-0.73): same u=0.4 now heads to ~0.44 vs ~0.60+ pre-change (E3 vs E9 0.174->0.406 in 270s), while u=0 cooling E8 matches E2; E10 0.417->0.496 in 130s at 0.55 implies y_ss~0.55 vs ~0.89 pre-change.

Change includes faster outflow / larger heat loss: would require faster u=0 cooling and lower ambient, but E8 final 0.157 vs E2 0.147 and similar decay shape argues against large increase; E10 rise rate also too small for faster loss alone.

Change includes slower response / larger dead-time: would require >100s flat after command change, but E8 fall starts within ~16-24s of u=0 and E9 rise within ~30-40s like pre-change, E10 responds within ~6-9s of 0.4->0.55, so delay is tens of s only.

Change includes sensor shift (offset/gain, not just noise): would shift all readings but preserve rise for +0.11 u and change scatter/ambient, but ambient ~0.15-0.16 unchanged, scatter +/-0.03 unchanged, and monitoring flat is explained by starting above new steady while u ramps.

Post-change gain K'~0.71-0.72 with ambient~0.157 implies new u* to hold 0.5 is ~0.47-0.50 (0.476 from (0.5-0.157)/0.72), vs pre 0.265; E9 y_ss(0.4)~0.44 and E10 y_ss(0.55)~0.55 bracket 0.5 but 130s hold is too short/noisy to pin within 0.02.
